findings.what_i_was_asked_to_verify: that 700 sits above every observed value in dev and held-out.
findings.what_i_found: FALSE. BODY_MAX is a stub cutoff, not an upper bound — the page-pointer candidate pool at any length reaches 1,010,422 chars (jpm-2024 item 15). Publishing that framing would have been a manufactured exemption.
findings.what_is_actually_true: A plateau argument, measured: 700 lies in an interval whose BOTH edges are dev values — nearest candidate below is intc-2002 item 5 at 629, nearest above is ibm-1997 item 5 at 805 — so every bound in 630..805 yields an identical dev result and no held-out value defines that interval. Held-out's own plateau is 248..738, far wider, so it cannot be what pinned 700. Exactly one held-out span sits inside the dev plateau: mrk-1995 item 8 at 738, whose body is 'incorporated by reference to pages 38 through 49 ... of the Company's 1995 Annual Report' — an external-document pointer the class rule rejects anyway, the same verdict its siblings 5 and 7 already get. So every figure D9 published is invariant across the entire dev-determined plateau. The constant was written once and never revised (single commit 4ecc1e5).
findings.limit_published_not_hidden: The dev plateau runs to 805 while held-out is unchanged only to 738. A different in-plateau choice (780) would have admitted mrk-1995 item 8 as a CANDIDATE — then rejected it, changing no published number. So 'any in-plateau value is equivalent' is true of D9's CONCLUSIONS, not of the candidate list. Stated in both the README and §g.
findings.min_refs_verdict: ledger-line-refs min_refs 9->11 is a ledger citation floor: not an extraction threshold, reads no filing, unrelated to any held-out label. Not the influence the rule targets.
